note: The +25% band is host load, but the explanation's claim that the wood changes add no measurable cost is false. Reviewer ran 7 interleaved make-perf legs in fresh detached worktrees (scratchpad/aud-base, aud-head; *aud374*.json). Reference totals: base 37.6/17.3/18.6 s, head 19.7/21.5/18.0/25.6 s. The quiet legs are level (head 18.0 vs base 17.3/18.6), and untouched stages move with the load. web/rest is level (base mean 0.231, head mean 0.231), so the serve.py fine lattice costs nothing measurable. (hinterland+woodland)/rest is 0.223-0.236 in all 3 base legs and 0.241-0.252 in all 4 head legs, and woodland goes from 0.00 to 0.52-0.64 s summed over 16 rows. So T11 wave 120's wood rule (wood_rank.py/parcels.py: tier-2 seats now ranked rather than dropped, low_by_the_water asked per seat) costs about +8% of hinterland+woodland, about +1.2% of the total. That is band 1 by itself, and the explanation denies it. Control batch3-cpu-interleaved timed base in a worktree against head in the clone, and its -9% comes from one cell (seed 4 at 10 hh: base 18.5/11.6/16.2 vs head 7.2/8.5/9.9 user-s); without that cell base 140.2 vs head 143.6 (+2.5%). Rewrite: host load for the band plus about 1.2% real in hinterland+woodland from T11, then band 2 on that.
